title: Mixing: Junior’s Farm by Wings | 1974
content:
Studio Three, Olympic Studios, London
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineer: Alan O’Duffy

A mixing session for Wings’ single ‘Junior’s Farm’ took place on 7 October 1974.

Paul McCartney had found the previous attempts – by Ernie Winfrey in Nashville and Geoff Emerick in London – unsatisfactory, and wanted to get it perfect for the release. He decided for this session to switch to a new mix engineer, Alan O’Duffy. He came recommended by MPL’s managing director Brian Brolly, who had worked with him on the rock opera Jesus Christ Superstar.

McCartney was impressed with O’Duffy’s mix, which arrived the next day on an acetate disc. However, more mixes were commissioned from George Martin, which were made on 11 October. McCartney ultimately chose O’Duffy’s for the single.
